title: Prove all-width input kernels for native full-frame histories (no new κ)
body:
## Result

The frozen native full-frame histories have an explicit input kernel at **every positive tensor width**. In logical native input coordinates, all backward observations are unchanged by `(X,Y,H) -> (X+v,Y+v,H)`; the forward observations are unchanged by `Y -> Y+v`. All helpers and owned inputs stay fixed. Thus the complete full-frame channel cannot exactly determine any nonconstant function of arbitrary original Y, even with arbitrary nonlinear postprocessing or unrestricted address-operator left combinations.

This strengthens the earlier scalar/finite-image result in this same PR. It is a source-specific information theorem with **no new κ**, paid profile, profitable caller or selected-frontier change.

| Frozen native body | Distinct nonzero full-frame histories | Kernel |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| #5402 raw backward | 4,891 | `[I; I; 0]` |
| final #4610 raw backward | 5,019 | `[I; I; 0]` |
| final #4610 raw forward | 4,968 | `[0; I; 0]` |

There are 112 X, 112 Y and 408 independent helper fields. The small backward certificate has 224 unit entries. The decisive identities are `H_f K=0` and `K_Y=I`; the backward channel may depend on X−Y, so this does not assert independence from Y when X is fixed.

## Review object and proof

The exact publication head is `be292a4c2724a17c7401bb736f969e898c43f0f2`. Review [KERNEL-PROOF.md](https://github.com/thu-nmrc/integer-mult-bounds/blob/be292a4c2724a17c7401bb736f969e898c43f0f2/research/physical-zqy-scalar-span/KERNEL-PROOF.md), [KERNEL.json](https://github.com/thu-nmrc/integer-mult-bounds/blob/be292a4c2724a17c7401bb736f969e898c43f0f2/research/physical-zqy-scalar-span/KERNEL.json), [KERNEL-RESULT.json](https://github.com/thu-nmrc/integer-mult-bounds/blob/be292a4c2724a17c7401bb736f969e898c43f0f2/research/physical-zqy-scalar-span/KERNEL-RESULT.json) and the [separate implementation's audit](https://github.com/thu-nmrc/integer-mult-bounds/blob/be292a4c2724a17c7401bb736f969e898c43f0f2/research/physical-zqy-scalar-span/INDEPENDENT-KERNEL-AUDIT.json).

- Fresh actual signed-native replay checks cancellation coefficient by coefficient in all three complete histories. No monomial-matrix independence, modular nonmembership, width-one sum relation or operator-polynomial inverse is needed.
- A separate native/group/frame implementation derives the provider kernel using exact Fraction elimination of scalar augmentations, then decisively verifies it against every **original operator-valued** history row. It imports neither the primary interpreter nor monomial/discovery code. Saved kernel rows are compared only after derivation.
- An alternate formal-word algebra reproduces all three identities using 72 free generator names and only adjacent inverse cancellation. It shares the source event interpreter and is explicitly corroboration, not an independent parser. Scalar coefficients remain outside tensor powers.
- Physical input displacements use the corresponding invertible birth frames. The common raw-backward full-frame factor is **R inverse**, with the retained conjugated letters. A zero logical history difference therefore remains zero physically; the argument does not claim free physical input preparation.

The nonidentifiability argument is ordinary linear algebra: input instances `z` and `z+Kv` have identical observations while Y varies arbitrarily. The contribution is the source-bound complete-channel identities and physical interpretation. The 13 MB module decomposition used during discovery is not shipped and is not a proof/runtime dependency.

## Exact scope

The observation data are only the retained full-nine-dimensional-frame values of each pinned native body, considered separately, including all versions after an intended exit. Original X/Y, partial-frame values/caches, extra paid transformations and changed words or input relations supply different information. Fixing helpers or owned values alone does not remove this kernel.

In particular, raw #5402 WORD ends with **eight nonzero partial-frame output caches**, before the provider boundary exchanges/clears them. They are excluded from this channel; the whole machine state is not claimed to hide Y. A provider-boundary extension must check any additional values explicitly. #5413's neutral completion is a changed paid-history resource and is not excluded here. The target `b=ZQY_return` uses the specified native return `Y_return=Dy`; a later caller Y contaminated by X is a different target. No finite-precision approximation lower bound is proved.

The earlier scalar/Gram/finite-ABI scripts and results remain byte-identical to initial head `6d81d47e6d107e3c52b4583526d31e102b219bdc` and remain optional direct replays. Their restricted numerical statements are not dependencies of the new kernel proof.

## Reproduction and validation

Python 3.12, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/physical-zqy-scalar-span
```

All **eight registered commands pass**, normally and with optimization: direct kernel, separate implementation, formal free-word corroboration and retained exact Clifford phase audit. The phase audit compares 147,456 native columns and 36,864 product columns. Explicit failure controls remain active under `-O`.

Committed-byte preflight passes for **31 package/input files** at this exact head. Official export and archive checks pass. All eight commands also pass in the exported **read-only, Git-free directory** (32 files including the export receipt), with files mode 0444, directories mode 0555, no Git on PATH, no .git directory, and identical pre/post inventory and SHA256 hashes. Archive SHA256: `6353e05f53e07c09bcb9df4996528305a8559a429b067455f7091a9b6b0ecbb2`. Local runtime is Python 3.12.13. The checkout is shallow; optional full-history ancestry preflight was not run. Direct base/publication ancestry passes.

The [hosted registered-package workflow](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40131113821) **passes at this exact final head**. The final follow-up commit only corrects the recorded local Python patch version; its scientific scripts and certificates are identical to the preceding proof commit, which also passed CI. This is reproducible replay evidence, not external scientific acceptance.

No selected cold replay, fresh complete native admission, compiler/outer, precision/tape/stock, Lean, Docker or complete multiplication-theorem audit is claimed. Internal AI-assisted corroboration and replay success remain distinct from external scientific acceptance.

The next constructive task must add genuinely different information: an exact partial-frame or changed paid interface with current-version ownership, all independent original inputs and a complete favorable observer/termination bill. Further postprocessing searches on this same frozen full-frame-only channel are stopped.
